title: StudySync Core ELA, Grade 6
edition: 2019-2021 national edition (Reading & Writing Companion printings 2020/2021; reviewed by EdReports as StudySync ELA 2021)

sources.what: McGraw Hill "StudySync ELA Grade Level Overview, Grade 6" PDF (2019), hosted by Montgomery County Public Schools: unit titles, essential questions, genre focus, every unit text, Extended Writing Project prompts, writing and grammar skills
EdReports review of StudySync ELA 2021, Grade 6, Gateway One: confirms the same six units and texts for the 2021 edition

summary: Grade 6 of McGraw Hill's StudySync Core ELA: six thematic units, each built around an essential question and a genre focus, mixing full texts and excerpts from novels, poems, plays, speeches and nonfiction. Students read through Skills, First Read and Close Read lessons and finish each unit with an Extended Writing Project covering narrative, argumentative, informative, literary analysis, oral presentation and research writing.

toc.label: Unit 1
toc.title: Testing Our Limits
toc.covers: Essential question "What do we do when life gets hard?"; genre focus fiction (plus a poem, a play and a memoir excerpt) about characters facing hardship; Extended Writing Project is a narrative story about an unexpected challenge on an ordinary day; grammar: personal pronouns, pronouns and antecedents, consistent pronoun use.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Eleven" (Sandra Cisneros)
children.covers: Short story: on her eleventh birthday Rachel is wrongly made to claim an ugly old sweater and breaks down in class; used to teach annotation, context clues and textual evidence.

children.label: Text
children.title: The Mighty Miss Malone (Christopher Paul Curtis), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: Deza Malone's family is uprooted by the Great Depression and travels by boxcar to find her father.

children.label: Text
children.title: Red Scarf Girl (Ji-Li Jiang), excerpt
children.covers: Memoir excerpt: a girl dedicated to the Communist Party faces interrogation during China's Cultural Revolution.

children.label: Text
children.title: Hatchet (Gary Paulsen), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: 13-year-old Brian is stranded in the Canadian wilderness after a plane crash; paired with Red Scarf Girl to compare setting.

children.label: Text
children.title: "The Magic Marker Mystery" (René Saldaña, Jr.)
children.covers: Mystery play: young investigator Mickey Rangel tracks down who is covering the school with graffiti; teaches dramatic elements and predictions.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Scout's Honor" (Avi)
children.covers: Short story: three Brooklyn Boy Scouts camp alone in the Palisades to prove they are tough and find it harder than expected; teaches plot structure.

children.label: Text
children.title: "The Good Samaritan" (René Saldaña, Jr.)
children.covers: Short story: teenage Rey faces a moral dilemma when his relationship with a neighbor family sours; teaches summarizing.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Jabberwocky" (Lewis Carroll)
children.covers: Nonsense poem of a heroic monster-slaying told in invented words; first of a three-text comparison across genres.

children.label: Text
children.title: Gathering Blue (Lois Lowry), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: Kira, who has a disabled leg, fears exile but her embroidery skill may earn her a place in her society.

children.label: Text
children.title: A Wrinkle in Time (Madeleine L'Engle), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: Meg, Charles Wallace and Calvin set out on a dangerous journey to find Meg's missing father.

toc.label: Unit 2
toc.title: You and Me
toc.covers: Essential question "How do relationships shape us?"; genre focus poetry, with stories and essays about family, mentors and friends; Extended Writing Project is an argumentative essay on whether relationships shape people's futures; grammar: basic spelling rules I, possessive pronouns, formal and informal language.

children.label: Text
children.title: Walk Two Moons (Sharon Creech), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: Sal blames herself for her mother leaving the family.

children.label: Text
children.title: Roll of Thunder, Hear My Cry (Mildred D. Taylor), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: a Black girl in the Depression-era South begins to confront racism with her family's support; teaches connotation, theme and story structure.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Teenagers" (Pat Mora)
children.covers: Poem: a mother watches her children turn into silent teenagers and then emerge as young adults.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Tableau" (Countee Cullen)
children.covers: Poem: two boys of different races walk together and draw stares, a picture of friendship across the color line.

children.label: Text
children.title: "The Voice in My Head" (Holly Warlick)
children.covers: Personal essay: a basketball player's tribute to a demanding coach after a rocky start.

children.label: Text
children.title: "We're on the Same Team" (Jacki Jing)
children.covers: Letter: a volleyball player answers a slight on her sport and says what it has taught her.

children.label: Text
children.title: "The Treasure of Lemon Brown" (Walter Dean Myers)
children.covers: Short story: Greg meets a homeless former bluesman whose "treasure" changes what Greg values; teaches point of view.

children.label: Text
children.title: The Circuit: Stories from the Life of a Migrant Child (Francisco Jiménez), excerpt
children.covers: Autobiographical fiction: a migrant child who moves constantly finds a mentor in a teacher.

children.label: Text
children.title: "That Day" (David Kherdian)
children.covers: Poem: the poet recalls a day with his father that shaped him.

children.label: Text
children.title: "A Poem for My Librarian, Mrs. Long" (Nikki Giovanni)
children.covers: Poem: a librarian in a segregated Southern town finds books for the young poet and changes her life.

toc.label: Unit 3
toc.title: In the Dark
toc.covers: Essential question "How do you know what to do when there are no instructions?"; genre focus informational text, with myths, novels and profiles of people acting without a guide; Extended Writing Project is an informative essay on what drives three people from the unit to act; grammar: parentheses, brackets and ellipses, prefixes, basic spelling rules II.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Heroes Every Child Should Know: Perseus" (Hamilton Wright Mabie)
children.covers: Greek myth retold: the tasks Perseus performs to become a hero.

children.label: Text
children.title: The Lightning Thief (Rick Riordan), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: a modern 12-year-old learns the Greek gods are part of his life.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Elena" (Pat Mora)
children.covers: Poem: an immigrant mother struggles to learn English so she will not lose touch with her children.

children.label: Text
children.title: Hatshepsut, His Majesty, Herself (Catherine M. Andronik), excerpt
children.covers: Informational text: the woman who took Egypt's throne in the 18th dynasty; teaches main idea and Greek and Latin affixes.

children.label: Text
children.title: "I, Too" (Langston Hughes)
children.covers: Harlem Renaissance poem protesting Black Americans' exclusion and claiming a place at the table.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Everybody Jump" from What If? (Randall Munroe)
children.covers: Science essay: what would happen if everyone on Earth jumped at once; teaches text structure and technical language.

children.label: Text
children.title: Hoot (Carl Hiaasen), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: Roy, new to Florida from Montana, runs into the school bully.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Donna O'Meara: The Volcano Lady" (McGraw Hill Education)
children.covers: Profile of a photographer who works at the rims of active volcanoes.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Dare to be Creative!" (Madeleine L'Engle)
children.covers: Speech urging young people to think for themselves and ask hard questions.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Margaret Bourke-White: Fearless Photographer" (McGraw Hill Education)
children.covers: Profile of the pioneering photojournalist and her persistence; teaches synthesizing.

toc.label: Unit 4
toc.title: Personal Best
toc.covers: Essential question "Which qualities of character matter most?"; genre focus argumentative text, with memoir, speeches, stories and paired opinion essays on courage and heroism; Extended Writing Project is a literary-analysis proposal arguing which two unit texts a school book club should read; grammar: commas with nonessential elements, using pronouns, commonly confused words.

children.label: Text
children.title: I Am Malala (Malala Yousafzai), excerpt
children.covers: Memoir excerpt: the Taliban close girls' schools in Pakistan and 11-year-old Malala's family fights for her education.

children.label: Text
children.title: Malala Yousafzai: Nobel Lecture
children.covers: Speech: the youngest Nobel Peace laureate sets out her cause of education for every child; teaches arguments and claims.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Priscilla and the Wimps" (Richard Peck)
children.covers: Humorous short story: a school bully gang meets its match when it targets Priscilla's friend.

children.label: Text
children.title: "All Summer in a Day" (Ray Bradbury)
children.covers: Science-fiction story: on rainy Venus, classmates lock Margot away during the one hour the sun appears in seven years.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Bullying in Schools" (StudySync)
children.covers: Paired argumentative essays: are schools doing enough about bullying; teaches claims, reasons and evidence.

children.label: Text
children.title: Freedom Walkers: The Story of the Montgomery Bus Boycott (Russell Freedman), excerpt
children.covers: Nonfiction: Claudette Colvin's stand before Rosa Parks in Montgomery.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Letter to Xavier High School" (Kurt Vonnegut)
children.covers: Letter urging students to make art, such as a poem written and then destroyed, for its own sake.

children.label: Text
children.title: Freedom's Daughters (Lynne Olson), excerpt
children.covers: Nonfiction: high-schooler Barbara Johns leads a protest over her segregated school in Farmville, Virginia.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Celebrities as Heroes" (StudySync)
children.covers: Paired opinion essays: should celebrities be called heroes.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Famous" (Naomi Shihab Nye)
children.covers: Poem asking what it really means to be famous.

toc.label: Unit 5
toc.title: Making Your Mark
toc.covers: Essential question "What's your story?"; genre focus drama, with plays, stories and memoir about identity, culture and loyalty; Extended Oral Project is an argumentative presentation on a belief the student holds, told through a personal story; grammar: reflexive and intensive pronouns, sentence variety, style.

children.label: Text
children.title: Warriors Don't Cry (Melba Pattillo Beals), excerpt
children.covers: Memoir excerpt: one of the Little Rock Nine on integrating Central High School in 1957.

children.label: Text
children.title: Damon and Pythias (Fan Kissen)
children.covers: Radio play from the Greek tale: a friend stakes his life on the condemned Pythias's return.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Amigo Brothers" (Piri Thomas)
children.covers: Short story: two best friends must box each other for a Golden Gloves spot.

children.label: Text
children.title: Listen, Slowly (Thanhhà Lai), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: 12-year-old Mai travels to Vietnam with her grandmother to learn her grandfather's fate.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Charles" (Shirley Jackson)
children.covers: Short story with a twist: a kindergartner's tales of a classmate's misbehavior.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Saying Yes" (Diana Chang)
children.covers: Poem about being both Chinese and American.

children.label: Text
children.title: "The All-American Slurp" (Lensey Namioka)
children.covers: Humorous story: a Chinese immigrant family's table manners clash with American customs.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Helen Keller" (Langston Hughes)
children.covers: Poem imagining how Helen Keller knew the world; first of three Helen Keller texts.

children.label: Text
children.title: The Story of My Life, Chapter IV (Helen Keller)
children.covers: Autobiography: the day Annie Sullivan arrived and Helen began to grasp language.

children.label: Text
children.title: The Miracle Worker (William Gibson), excerpt
children.covers: Play excerpt: Annie Sullivan insists Helen be held to higher standards to learn.

toc.label: Unit 6
toc.title: True to Yourself
toc.covers: Essential question "Who are you meant to be?"; genre focus realistic fiction, with novels, profiles of young innovators and three accounts of Rosa Parks; Extended Writing Project is a research report on a topic drawn from the unit; grammar: dashes and hyphens, quotation marks and italics, run-on sentences.

children.label: Text
children.title: Bronx Masquerade (Nikki Grimes), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: Bronx teenagers reveal their true selves through poetry in class.

children.label: Text
children.title: "A BEACON of Hope: The Story of Hannah Herbst" (Rebecca Harrington)
children.covers: Profile of a teenage inventor of an ocean-energy device.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Shree Bose: Never Too Young to Change the World" (Amanda Sperber)
children.covers: Profile of a teenager whose cancer research won the Google Science Fair.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Letter to His Daughter" (W.E.B. Du Bois)
children.covers: Letter of advice to his daughter studying abroad; teaches figurative language.

children.label: Text
children.title: "The Story Behind the Bus" (The Henry Ford)
children.covers: Nonfiction account of Rosa Parks's 1955 arrest; one of three Parks texts compared.

children.label: Text
children.title: "Rosa" (Rita Dove)
children.covers: Poem capturing Rosa Parks in the moment of her refusal.

children.label: Text
children.title: Rosa Parks: My Story (Rosa Parks), excerpt
children.covers: Autobiography: Parks's own account of the bus arrest; compared with the two other versions.

children.label: Text
children.title: Eleanor Roosevelt: A Life of Discovery (Russell Freedman), excerpt
children.covers: Biography: a shy, reluctant first lady finds her own public voice.

children.label: Text
children.title: Brave (Svetlana Chmakova), excerpt
children.covers: Graphic novel excerpt: a bullied middle schooler daydreams of heroics.

children.label: Text
children.title: I Never Had It Made (Jackie Robinson), excerpt
children.covers: Autobiography: Robinson on the abuse he faced breaking baseball's color line.

children.label: Text
children.title: Touching Spirit Bear (Ben Mikaelsen), excerpt
children.covers: Novel excerpt: angry teenager Cole chooses survival alone in the Alaskan wilderness over prison.

notes: No ISBN on the school list; assumed to be the same 2019-2021 national edition as Grades 7 and 8 (match is exact under that assumption). Each unit is printed as its own consumable Reading & Writing Companion volume (Unit 1 to Unit 6, per the retailer listings); the digital platform carries further texts, Blasts, StudySyncTV episodes and English Language Learner resources (general). Every unit ends in an Extended Writing Project (one unit per grade uses an Extended Oral Project instead) taught through Plan, Draft, Revise, Edit and Publish steps (page). Texts listed here are the unit selections named in the McGraw Hill Grade Level Overview; several are excerpts from full-length books, and some (marked Independent Read in the program) are read without full lesson support. EdReports also lists Alice's Adventures in Wonderland among Unit 4 texts in the 2021 review; the Overview does not.
